findings.evidence: The notification-settings form has a submit button labeled 'Save', but the artifact defines no next state describing what the user sees after clicking it: no confirmation, no result message, no updated display, and no navigation to a new state.
findings.fix: Specify what the user sees after clicking Save: either a success message on the same screen, a navigation to a confirmation state, or an updated form state that shows the save completed.
findings.location: the notification-settings section, the notification-settings form and its submit button
findings.violation: A save action's result feedback is not specified in the artifact, so the user cannot tell whether the save completed, failed, or is still processing.

findings.evidence: the "invite-sent" section defines 0 controls whose target names another defined state (1 incoming link from elsewhere in the artifact).
findings.fix: Add a control inside the "invite-sent" section whose target is another state the artifact defines, for example a back, cancel, or continue control.
findings.violation: This state offers no control whose target names another state the artifact defines, so a user who reaches it has no path to leave it within the artifact.

findings.evidence: The archive-confirm section states 'You can restore it at any time from the archived projects list', but the artifact defines no screen called 'archived projects list' or any state where users can view or restore archived projects. The restoration path exists in the described product but not in the artifact's state graph.
findings.fix: Either define an archived projects list screen in the artifact and link to it from relevant states, or remove the mention of restoration if the feature is not part of this design.
findings.location: the archive-confirm section, the confirmation message text; the artifact as a whole lacks the archived projects list state
findings.violation: The reversal path for an archivable action is mentioned in text but the screen where reversal occurs is not defined in the artifact, so the user cannot navigate to it.

findings.evidence: In the workspace-overview section, the promo text uses 'teammates' ('Invite 3 teammates this month...'). In the project-settings section, the action is labeled 'Invite a team member'. Both refer to the same action and concept, but use different terminology without explanation.
findings.fix: Use one consistent term throughout the artifact for this concept, such as either 'team member' or 'teammate' in all places where it appears.
findings.location: the workspace-overview section (promo text) and the invite-member section (heading)
findings.violation: Two different terms name the same concept (team members to invite) with no cue that they refer to the same thing, creating inconsistency in how the artifact names the core action.

findings.evidence: <button> with no text content and no accessible-name attribute
findings.fix: Add visible text to this control, or an aria-label attribute naming what it does.
findings.violation: This control has neither visible text nor an accessible-name attribute, so nothing on screen names what the control does.
